questions.prompt: Which analysis paths should get retrieval-augmented chunking?
questions.description: Currently the CLI path (`insights check --analyze`) sends the entire conversation raw. The server path (`analyzeSession`) already does naive token-based chunking. Which paths get the upgrade?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Both CLI and server paths, since they share the same underlying analysis prompts and should produce consistent results.

questions.prompt: What should drive the chunking boundaries?
questions.description: The current `chunkMessages()` splits purely by token count. The existing `chunkText()` splits by delimiters. What boundaries make sense for conversation analysis?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Role-boundary chunking: each chunk spans a logical exchange (user turn + assistant response + tool results), annotated with role labels, timestamps, and tool context. This preserves conversational semantics that token-count splitting destroys.

questions.prompt: When should retrieval kick in vs. sending the full conversation?
questions.description: Short conversations don't need retrieval — they fit in the prompt. At what point should the system switch from 'send everything' to 'retrieve relevant chunks'?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Threshold-based: when estimated tokens exceed 80% of the model's context window (similar to the existing `MAX_INPUT_TOKENS` check), switch to retrieval mode. Below that, send everything for maximum fidelity.

questions.prompt: When should conversation chunks get embedded?
questions.description: The existing `backfillEmbeddings` embeds messages as raw content. For retrieval-augmented analysis, chunks need to be embedded with their annotated context (role, tools, timestamps). When does this happen?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Embed on-demand at analysis time: when `insights check --analyze` runs and the conversation exceeds the threshold, chunk + embed + retrieve in one pass. No background embedding job needed — the chunks are ephemeral to the analysis session.

questions.prompt: What drives the retrieval query — what gets embedded and searched against?
questions.description: For similarity search, we need a query vector and corpus vectors. What should they represent?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Hybrid: embed each conversation chunk with its annotated text (role + content + tools). For the query, embed the analysis instructions + session metadata + any related insights as the query vector. This retrieves chunks most relevant to what the analyzer is looking for.

options.label: Embed raw message content, query with analysis prompt
Embed annotated chunks (role+content+tools), query with analysis prompt
Annotated chunks + combined query (instructions + metadata + related insights)

questions.prompt: How should retrieved chunks be augmented before sending to the LLM?
questions.description: Raw chunks lack conversation flow context. How much surrounding context should each retrieved chunk carry?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Window augmentation: each retrieved chunk gets prepended with a compact conversation summary (from `formatMessagesForAnalysis` of preceding messages) and tagged with its position in the full conversation (e.g., 'turn 12 of 45'). This gives the LLM orientation without re-inflating the prompt.

questions.prompt: The current server path runs a separate facet extraction pass on the full conversation. How should this work with retrieval?
questions.description: Facets (outcome_satisfaction, workflow_pattern) are holistic — they can't be merged across chunks. How should retrieval handle them?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Keep the facet pass separate: use retrieval for the main analysis (decisions, learnings, friction), but for facets, use a truncated summary of the full conversation (first/last/middle samples) since facets need global view. This matches the existing pattern where facets already get a separate truncated pass.

options.label: Separate pass with sampled summary (existing pattern)

questions.prompt: What should happen if embeddings aren't available (no Ollama, no vector extension, backfill not run)?
questions.description: The existing code falls back gracefully in many places. How should this feature handle missing infrastructure?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Graceful degradation: if embeddings aren't available, fall back to the current naive token-count chunking (server path) or truncation (CLI path). Log a warning suggesting `code-insights embeddings backfill`. Never block analysis on missing embeddings.

options.label: Error with instructions to set up embeddings
Auto-setup: prompt to install Ollama + run backfill

questions.prompt: Should this reuse the existing `vec_messages` vector table or create a new one?
questions.description: The existing backfill embeds raw message content into `vec_messages`. The new system needs annotated chunks with role/tool context. These are different embeddings.
questions.recommendedAnswer: New table `vec_analysis_chunks`: the existing `vec_messages` embeds raw content for cross-session search. Analysis chunks are ephemeral, annotated, and session-scoped. Separate tables keep concerns clean and avoid re-embedding existing data.

options.label: Reuse vec_messages (add annotation to source text)
